name: z_Terraform Plan (Reusable)

# Reusable workflow for running Terraform plan in service repositories
# Supports private Terraform modules via GitHub App authentication
on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      working_directory:
        description: 'Terraform directory to plan'
        required: true
        type: string
      terraform_version:
        description: 'Terraform version to use'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: '1.7.4'
      environment:
        description: 'Environment name (dev, qa, prod)'
        required: true
        type: string
      comment_on_pr:
        description: 'Post plan summary as PR comment'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: true
      upload_artifact:
        description: 'Upload plan file as artifact'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
    secrets:
      TERRAFORM_MODULES_APP_ID:
        description: 'GitHub App ID for private module access'
        required: false
      TERRAFORM_MODULES_APP_PRIVATE_KEY:
        description: 'GitHub App private key for private module access'
        required: false
    outputs:
      plan_status:
        description: 'Plan status (success, failure, or no_changes)'
        value: ${{ jobs.plan.outputs.status }}
      changes_detected:
        description: 'Whether changes were detected (true/false)'
        value: ${{ jobs.plan.outputs.changes_detected }}
      add_count:
        description: 'Number of resources to add'
        value: ${{ jobs.plan.outputs.add_count }}
      change_count:
        description: 'Number of resources to change'
        value: ${{ jobs.plan.outputs.change_count }}
      destroy_count:
        description: 'Number of resources to destroy'
        value: ${{ jobs.plan.outputs.destroy_count }}

permissions:
  id-token: write
  contents: read
  pull-requests: write

jobs:
  plan:
    name: Terraform Plan
    runs-on: static-ip-runner
    environment: ${{ inputs.environment }}
    outputs:
      status: ${{ steps.plan-result.outputs.status }}
      changes_detected: ${{ steps.plan-result.outputs.changes_detected }}
      add_count: ${{ steps.extract-stats.outputs.add_count }}
      change_count: ${{ steps.extract-stats.outputs.change_count }}
      destroy_count: ${{ steps.extract-stats.outputs.destroy_count }}

    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Setup Terraform
        uses: hashicorp/setup-terraform@v3
        with:
          terraform_version: ${{ inputs.terraform_version }}
          terraform_wrapper: false

      - name: Configure GCP Auth
        id: gcp-auth-config
        run: |
          # Read from calling repo's environment variables
          PROJECT_NUMBER="${{ vars.GCP_PROJECT_NUMBER }}"
          SERVICE_NAME="${{ vars.SERVICE_NAME }}"

          if [ -z "$PROJECT_NUMBER" ] || [ -z "$SERVICE_NAME" ]; then
            echo "::error::Missing required environment variables."
            echo "::error::Set GCP_PROJECT_NUMBER and SERVICE_NAME as GitHub Environment variables for '${{ inputs.environment }}'."
            exit 1
          fi

          ENV="${{ inputs.environment }}"
          POOL_ID="github-${SERVICE_NAME}-${ENV}"
          PROVIDER="projects/${PROJECT_NUMBER}/locations/global/workloadIdentityPools/${POOL_ID}/providers/github-provider"

          # Allow explicit GKE project ID override (e.g., shared env uses shr abbreviation)
          GKE_PROJECT="${{ vars.GCP_GKE_PROJECT_ID }}"
          if [ -z "$GKE_PROJECT" ]; then
            GKE_PROJECT="kd-ix-eur-${ENV}-gke"
          fi
          SA="${POOL_ID}@${GKE_PROJECT}.iam.gserviceaccount.com"

          echo "provider_id=${PROVIDER}" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          echo "service_account=${SA}" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          echo "Using WIF pool: ${POOL_ID} (project ${PROJECT_NUMBER})"
          echo "Service account: ${SA}"

      - name: Authenticate to GCP
        uses: google-github-actions/auth@v2
        with:
          workload_identity_provider: ${{ steps.gcp-auth-config.outputs.provider_id }}
          service_account: ${{ steps.gcp-auth-config.outputs.service_account }}

      - name: Setup Cloud SDK
        uses: google-github-actions/setup-gcloud@v2

      - name: Generate GitHub App Token
        id: app-token
        uses: actions/create-github-app-token@v1
        continue-on-error: true
        with:
          app-id: ${{ secrets.TERRAFORM_MODULES_APP_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.TERRAFORM_MODULES_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          owner: konecta-ix-platform

      - name: Configure Git for Private Modules
        if: steps.app-token.outcome == 'success'
        run: |
          git config --global url."https://x-access-token:${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token }}@github.com/".insteadOf "https://github.com/"
          echo "Configured git for private module access"

      - name: Terraform Init
        run: terraform init
        working-directory: ${{ inputs.working_directory }}

      - name: Terraform Plan
        id: plan
        run: |
          terraform plan -out=tfplan -no-color 2>&1 | tee plan_output.txt
          EXIT_CODE=${PIPESTATUS[0]}
          echo "exit_code=$EXIT_CODE" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          exit $EXIT_CODE
        working-directory: ${{ inputs.working_directory }}
        continue-on-error: true

      - name: Terraform Show
        id: show
        if: steps.plan.outcome == 'success'
        run: |
          terraform show -no-color tfplan > plan_readable.txt
          head -n 50 plan_readable.txt > plan_summary.txt
        working-directory: ${{ inputs.working_directory }}

      - name: Check for changes
        id: check-changes
        if: steps.plan.outcome == 'success'
        run: |
          if grep -q "No changes" plan_readable.txt; then
            echo "changes_detected=false" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          else
            echo "changes_detected=true" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          fi
        working-directory: ${{ inputs.working_directory }}

      - name: Extract plan statistics
        id: extract-stats
        if: steps.plan.outcome == 'success'
        run: |
          ADD_COUNT=$(grep -oP 'Plan: \K\d+(?= to add)' plan_output.txt || echo "0")
          CHANGE_COUNT=$(grep -oP '\K\d+(?= to change)' plan_output.txt || echo "0")
          DESTROY_COUNT=$(grep -oP '\K\d+(?= to destroy)' plan_output.txt || echo "0")

          cat > plan_stats_${{ inputs.environment }}.json <<EOF
          {
            "directory": "${{ inputs.working_directory }}",
            "environment": "${{ inputs.environment }}",
            "status": "success",
            "add": ${ADD_COUNT},
            "change": ${CHANGE_COUNT},
            "destroy": ${DESTROY_COUNT}
          }
          EOF

          echo "add_count=${ADD_COUNT}" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          echo "change_count=${CHANGE_COUNT}" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          echo "destroy_count=${DESTROY_COUNT}" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
        working-directory: ${{ inputs.working_directory }}

      - name: Create failure statistics
        if: steps.plan.outcome == 'failure'
        run: |
          cat > plan_stats_${{ inputs.environment }}.json <<EOF
          {
            "directory": "${{ inputs.working_directory }}",
            "environment": "${{ inputs.environment }}",
            "status": "failure",
            "add": 0,
            "change": 0,
            "destroy": 0
          }
          EOF
        working-directory: ${{ inputs.working_directory }}

      - name: Upload plan statistics
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: plan-stats-${{ inputs.environment }}-${{ hashFiles(inputs.working_directory) }}
          path: ${{ inputs.working_directory }}/plan_stats_${{ inputs.environment }}.json
          retention-days: 7

      - name: Comment on PR
        if: inputs.comment_on_pr && github.event_name == 'pull_request' && steps.plan.outcome == 'success'
        uses: actions/github-script@v7
        with:
          script: |
            const fs = require('fs');
            const planSummary = fs.readFileSync('${{ inputs.working_directory }}/plan_summary.txt', 'utf8');
            const planOutput = fs.readFileSync('${{ inputs.working_directory }}/plan_output.txt', 'utf8');

            const addMatch = planOutput.match(/Plan: (\d+) to add/);
            const changeMatch = planOutput.match(/(\d+) to change/);
            const destroyMatch = planOutput.match(/(\d+) to destroy/);

            const toAdd = addMatch ? addMatch[1] : '0';
            const toChange = changeMatch ? changeMatch[1] : '0';
            const toDestroy = destroyMatch ? destroyMatch[1] : '0';

            const body = `## Terraform Plan: \`${{ inputs.working_directory }}\`

            **Environment:** ${{ inputs.environment }}
            **Changes:** ${toAdd} to add, ${toChange} to change, ${toDestroy} to destroy

            <details>
            <summary>Show Plan</summary>

            \`\`\`terraform
            ${planSummary}
            \`\`\`

            </details>

            *Plan generated at: ${new Date().toISOString()}*
            `;

            github.rest.issues.createComment({
              issue_number: context.issue.number,
              owner: context.repo.owner,
              repo: context.repo.repo,
              body: body
            });

      - name: Upload plan artifact
        id: upload-plan
        if: inputs.upload_artifact && steps.plan.outcome == 'success'
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: tfplan-${{ inputs.environment }}-${{ hashFiles(inputs.working_directory) }}
          path: ${{ inputs.working_directory }}/tfplan
          retention-days: 30

      - name: Plan Result
        id: plan-result
        if: always()
        run: |
          if [ "${{ steps.plan.outcome }}" == "failure" ]; then
            echo "status=failure" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
            echo "changes_detected=false" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
            exit 1
          elif [ "${{ steps.check-changes.outputs.changes_detected }}" == "false" ]; then
            echo "status=no_changes" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
            echo "changes_detected=false" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          else
            echo "status=success" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
            echo "changes_detected=true" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          fi

      - name: Summary
        if: always()
        run: |
          echo "## [${{ inputs.environment }}] Terraform Plan" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
          echo "" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
          echo "**Directory:** \`${{ inputs.working_directory }}\`" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
          echo "**Environment:** ${{ inputs.environment }}" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
          echo "" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY

          if [ "${{ steps.plan.outcome }}" == "success" ]; then
            if [ "${{ steps.check-changes.outputs.changes_detected }}" == "true" ]; then
              echo "**Plan Status:** Changes detected" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
              echo "- **Changes:** ${{ steps.extract-stats.outputs.add_count }} to add, ${{ steps.extract-stats.outputs.change_count }} to change, ${{ steps.extract-stats.outputs.destroy_count }} to destroy" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
              echo "" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
              echo "<details>" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
              echo "<summary>Plan Output (first 50 lines)</summary>" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
              echo "" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
              echo "\`\`\`terraform" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
              sed '' plan_summary.txt >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY || cat plan_summary.txt >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
              echo "\`\`\`" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
              echo "</details>" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
            else
              echo "**Plan Status:** No changes" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
            fi
          else
            echo "**Plan Status:** Failed" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
          fi
        working-directory: ${{ inputs.working_directory }}
```

> AGENT

The reusable `terraform-plan.yml` runs `terraform plan` without any `env:` block mapping secrets to `TF_VAR_*` environment variables. It has `environment: ${{ inputs.environment }}` so it can access GitHub Environment secrets, but there's no step that injects them as shell environment variables for Terraform.

The calling workflow also doesn't pass `secrets: inherit`, so the reusable workflow can only see its own declared secrets (`TERRAFORM_MODULES_APP_ID` and `TERRAFORM_MODULES_APP_PRIVATE_KEY`).

Two options to fix this:

**Option A** - Update the shared reusable workflow to auto-export `TF_VAR_*` secrets (best long-term fix, works for all repos):

Add a step before `terraform plan` that extracts all secrets prefixed with `TF_VAR_`:
```yaml
- name: Export TF_VAR secrets
  env:
    ALL_SECRETS: ${{ toJSON(secrets) }}
  run: |
    echo "$ALL_SECRETS" | jq -r 'to_entries[] | select(.key | startswith("TF_VAR_")) | "\(.key)=\(.value)"' >> $GITHUB_ENV
```
Plus `secrets: inherit` on the calling side.

**Option B** - Inline the plan/apply jobs in this repo's workflow with explicit `env:` blocks (quick fix, this repo only).

Which approach do you prefer?

            echo "::error::Set GCP_PROJECT_NUMBER and SERVICE_NAME as GitHub Environment variables for '${{ inputs.environment }}'."

          SA="${POOL_ID}@${GKE_PROJECT}.iam.gserviceaccount.com"

          echo "provider_id=${PROVIDER}" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          echo "service_account=${SA}" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          echo "Using WIF pool: ${POOL_ID} (project ${PROJECT_NUMBER})"
          echo "Service account: ${SA}"

      - name: Authenticate to GCP
        uses: google-github-actions/auth@v2
        with:
          workload_identity_provider: ${{ steps.gcp-auth-config.outputs.provider_id }}
          service_account: ${{ steps.gcp-auth-config.outputs.service_account }}

      - name: Setup Cloud SDK
        uses: google-github-actions/setup-gcloud@v2

      - name: Generate GitHub App Token
        id: app-token
        uses: actions/create-github-app-token@v1
        continue-on-error: true
        with:
          app-id: ${{ secrets.TERRAFORM_MODULES_APP_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.TERRAFORM_MODULES_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          owner: konecta-ix-platform

      - name: Configure Git for Private Modules
        if: steps.app-token.outcome == 'success'
        run: |
          git config --global url."https://x-access-token:${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token }}@github.com/".insteadOf "https://github.com/"
          echo "Configured git for private module access"

      - name: Terraform Init
        run: terraform init
        working-directory: ${{ inputs.working_directory }}

      - name: Pre-Apply Validation
        run: terraform validate
        working-directory: ${{ inputs.working_directory }}

      - name: Fresh Plan (Pre-Apply)
        id: pre-plan
        run: |
          echo "Generating fresh plan to catch any drift..."
          terraform plan -out=tfplan -no-color 2>&1 | tee pre_plan_output.txt

          if grep -q "No changes" pre_plan_output.txt; then
            echo "has_changes=false" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
            echo "::warning::No changes detected in fresh plan. Deployment may be unnecessary."
          else
            echo "has_changes=true" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          fi
        working-directory: ${{ inputs.working_directory }}

      - name: Terraform Apply
        id: apply
        if: steps.pre-plan.outputs.has_changes == 'true'
        run: |
          terraform apply -auto-approve tfplan 2>&1 | tee apply_output.txt
          APPLY_EXIT_CODE=${PIPESTATUS[0]}
          echo "exit_code=$APPLY_EXIT_CODE" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          exit $APPLY_EXIT_CODE
        working-directory: ${{ inputs.working_directory }}
        continue-on-error: true

      - name: Skip Apply (No Changes)
        if: steps.pre-plan.outputs.has_changes == 'false'
        run: |
          echo "Skipping apply - no changes detected"
          echo "exit_code=0" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

      - name: Capture Outputs
        id: outputs
        if: steps.apply.outputs.exit_code == '0' || steps.pre-plan.outputs.has_changes == 'false'
        run: |
          terraform output -json > outputs.json
          {
            echo 'json<<EOF'
            cat outputs.json
            echo EOF
          } >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
        working-directory: ${{ inputs.working_directory }}

      - name: Post-Apply Validation
        if: steps.apply.outputs.exit_code == '0'
        run: |
          echo "Running post-apply validation..."
          terraform plan -detailed-exitcode -no-color || {
            EXIT_CODE=$?
            if [ $EXIT_CODE -eq 2 ]; then
              echo "::warning::Post-apply plan detected drift. This may indicate resource drift or provider issues."
            fi
          }
        working-directory: ${{ inputs.working_directory }}
        continue-on-error: true

      - name: Deployment Timestamp
        id: timestamp
        run: |
          echo "deployment_time=$(date -u +"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

      - name: Generate Artifact Name
        id: artifact-name
        run: |
          SANITIZED=$(echo "${{ inputs.working_directory }}" | tr '/' '-')
          echo "name=terraform-apply-${{ inputs.environment }}-${SANITIZED}-${{ github.run_id }}" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

      - name: Upload Apply Output
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: ${{ steps.artifact-name.outputs.name }}
          path: |
            ${{ inputs.working_directory }}/apply_output.txt
            ${{ inputs.working_directory }}/outputs.json
          retention-days: 90

      - name: Apply Result
        id: apply-result
        if: always()
        run: |
          if [ "${{ steps.pre-plan.outputs.has_changes }}" == "false" ]; then
            echo "status=success" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
            echo "No changes to apply"
          elif [ "${{ steps.apply.outputs.exit_code }}" == "0" ]; then
            echo "status=success" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
            echo "Apply completed successfully"
          else
            echo "status=failure" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
            echo "::error::Apply failed"
            exit 1
          fi

      - name: Summary
        if: always()
        run: |
          echo "## Terraform Apply Summary" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
          echo "" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
          echo "**Directory:** \`${{ inputs.working_directory }}\`" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
          echo "**Environment:** ${{ inputs.environment }}" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
          echo "**Deployment Time:** ${{ steps.timestamp.outputs.deployment_time }}" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
          echo "" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY

          if [ "${{ steps.pre-plan.outputs.has_changes }}" == "false" ]; then
            echo "**Status:** No changes detected (skipped apply)" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
          elif [ "${{ steps.apply.outputs.exit_code }}" == "0" ]; then
            echo "**Status:** Applied successfully" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
            echo "" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
            echo "<details>" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
            echo "<summary>Terraform Outputs</summary>" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
            echo "" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
            echo "\`\`\`json" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
            cat outputs.json >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
            echo "\`\`\`" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
            echo "</details>" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
          else
            echo "**Status:** Apply failed" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
          fi
        working-directory: ${{ inputs.working_directory }}
```

then\n            echo \"- $ADD to add, $CHANGE to change, $DESTROY to destroy\" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY\n          else\n            echo \"- No infrastructure changes\" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY\n          fi\n          echo \"\" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY\n\n          echo \"**Job Results:**\" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY\n          echo \"- Validation: ${{ needs.validate.result }}\" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY\n          echo \"- Plan: ${{ needs.plan.result }}\" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY\n          echo \"- Review: ${{ needs.review-gate.result }}\" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY\n          echo \"- Apply: ${{ needs.apply.result }}\" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY\n          echo \"\" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY\n\n          if [ \"${{ needs.apply.result }}\" == \"failure\" ]; then\n            echo \"**Deployment failed** - Review error logs in apply job above\" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY\n          elif [ \"${{ needs.review-gate.result }}\" == \"failure\" ]; then\n            echo \"**Deployment cancelled** - Plan was not approved during review\" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY\n          elif [ \"${{ needs.apply.result }}\" == \"skipped\" ];    423→          if [ "${{ steps.pre-plan.outputs.has_changes }}" == "false" ]; then
   424→            echo "status=success" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
   425→          elif [ "${{ steps.apply.outputs.exit_code }}" == "0" ]; then
   426→            echo "status=success" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
   427→          else
   428→            echo "status=failure" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
   429→            echo "::error::Apply failed"
   430→            exit 1
   431→          fi
   432→
   433→  summary:
   434→    name: Deployment Summary
   435→    needs: [pre-flight, validate, plan, review-gate, apply]
   436→    if: always()
   437→    runs-on: static-ip-runner
   438→    steps:
   439→      - name: Generate Summary
   440→        run: |
   441→          echo "## Terraform Deployment Summary" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
   442→          echo "" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
   443→
   444→          OVERALL_STATUS="Deployed"
   445→          if [ "${{ needs.apply.result }}" == "failure" ]; then
   446→            OVERALL_STATUS="Failed"
   447→          elif [ "${{ needs.review-gate.result }}" == "failure" ]; then
   448→            OVERALL_STATUS="Cancelled"
   449→          elif [ "${{ needs.apply.result }}" == "skipped" ]; then
   450→            OVERALL_STATUS="Skipped"
   451→          fi
   452→
   453→          echo "### Overall Status: $OVERALL_STATUS" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
   454→          echo "" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
   455→          echo "**Environment:** ${{ inputs.environment }}" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
   456→          echo "**Directory:** \`${{ needs.pre-flight.outputs.working_directory }}\`" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
   457→          echo "" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
   458→
   459→          ADD="${{ needs.plan.outputs.add_count || '0' }}"
   460→          CHANGE="${{ needs.plan.outputs.change_count || '0' }}"
   461→          DESTROY="${{ needs.plan.outputs.destroy_count || '0' }}"
   462→
   463→          echo "**Changes Applied:**" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
   464→          if [ "$ADD" != "0" ] || [ "$CHANGE" != "0" ] || [ "$DESTROY" != "0" ]; then
   465→            echo "- $ADD to add, $CHANGE to change, $DESTROY to destroy" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
   466→          else
   467→            echo "- No infrastructure changes" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
   468→          fi
   469→          echo "" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
   470→
   471→          echo "**Job Results:**" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
   472→          echo "- Validation: ${{ needs.validate.result }}" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
   473→          echo "- Plan: ${{ needs.plan.result }}" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
   474→          echo "- Review: ${{ needs.review-gate.result }}" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
   475→          echo "- Apply: ${{ needs.apply.result }}" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
   476→          echo "" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
   477→
   478→          if [ "${{ needs.apply.result }}" == "failure" ]; then
   479→            echo "**Deployment failed** - Review error logs in apply job above" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
   480→          elif [ "${{ needs.review-gate.result }}" == "failure" ]; then
   481→            echo "**Deployment cancelled** - Plan was not approved during review" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
   482→          elif [ "${{ needs.apply.result }}" == "skipped" ]; then
   483→            echo "**Deployment skipped** - Check previous job failures" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
   484→          else
   485→            echo "**Deployment complete** - Infrastructure updated for ${{ inputs.environment }}" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
   486→          fi
   487→
   488→      - name: Check Overall Status
   489→        if: needs.apply.result == 'failure'
   490→        run: |
   491→          echo "::error::Deployment failed. Check the apply job logs for details."
   492→          exit 1
   493→

     1→name: Auto Validate and Plan
     2→
     3→# Triggers on pull requests to validate Terraform changes before merge
     4→on:
     5→  pull_request:
     6→    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened]
     7→    branches:
     8→      - main
     9→      - develop
    10→    paths:
    11→      - 'environments/**/*.tf'
    12→      - 'environments/**/*.tfvars'
    13→
    14→concurrency:
    15→  group: pr-${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
    16→  cancel-in-progress: true
    17→
    18→permissions:
    19→  id-token: write
    20→  contents: read
    21→  pull-requests: write
    22→
    23→jobs:
    24→  detect-changes:
    25→    name: Detect Changed Directories
    26→    runs-on: static-ip-runner
    27→    outputs:
    28→      matrix: ${{ steps.set-matrix.outputs.matrix }}
    29→      has_changes: ${{ steps.set-matrix.outputs.has_changes }}
    30→
    31→    steps:
    32→      - name: Checkout code
    33→        uses: actions/checkout@v4
    34→        with:
    35→          fetch-depth: 0
    36→
    37→      - name: Get changed Terraform directories
    38→        id: changed-files
    39→        run: |
    40→          git diff --name-only origin/${{ github.base_ref }}...HEAD \
    41→            | grep -E '^environments/[^/]+/terraform/.*\.tf$' \
    42→            > tf_files.txt || true
    43→
    44→          cat tf_files.txt | xargs -I{} dirname {} | sort -u > directories.txt
    45→
    46→          echo "Changed directories:"
    47→          cat directories.txt
    48→
    49→      - name: Build matrix
    50→        id: set-matrix
    51→        run: |
    52→          if [ -s directories.txt ]; then
    53→            MATRIX=$(while IFS= read -r dir; do
    54→              env=$(echo "$dir" | cut -d'/' -f2)
    55→              echo "$dir|$env"
    56→            done < directories.txt | jq -R -s -c '
    57→              split("\n") |
    58→              map(select(length > 0)) |
    59→              map(split("|") | {directory: .[0], environment: .[1]})
    60→            ')
    61→
    62→            echo "matrix=$MATRIX" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
    63→            echo "has_changes=true" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
    64→            echo "Will validate matrix: $MATRIX"
    65→          else
    66→            echo "matrix=[]" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
    67→            echo "has_changes=false" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
    68→            echo "No Terraform changes to validate"
    69→          fi
    70→
    71→  validate:
    72→    name: Validate (${{ matrix.environment }})
    73→    needs: detect-changes
    74→    if: needs.detect-changes.outputs.has_changes == 'true'
    75→    strategy:
    76→      matrix:
    77→        include: ${{ fromJson(needs.detect-changes.outputs.matrix) }}
    78→      fail-fast: false
    79→    uses: konecta-ix-services/.github-private/.github/workflows/terraform-validate.yml@main
    80→    with:
    81→      working_directory: ${{ matrix.directory }}
    82→      terraform_version: '1.13.5'
    83→      enable_trivy: true
    84→      trivy_severity: 'MEDIUM'
    85→
    86→  plan:
    87→    name: Plan (${{ matrix.environment }})
    88→    needs: [detect-changes, validate]
    89→    if: needs.detect-changes.outputs.has_changes == 'true'
    90→    strategy:
    91→      matrix:
    92→        include: ${{ fromJson(needs.detect-changes.outputs.matrix) }}
    93→      fail-fast: false
    94→    uses: konecta-ix-services/.github-private/.github/workflows/terraform-plan.yml@main
    95→    with:
    96→      working_directory: ${{ matrix.directory }}
    97→      terraform_version: '1.13.5'
    98→      environment: ${{ matrix.environment }}
    99→      comment_on_pr: true
   100→      upload_artifact: false
   101→
   102→  summary:
   103→    name: Validation Summary
   104→    needs: [detect-changes, validate, plan]
   105→    if: always()
   106→    runs-on: static-ip-runner
   107→    steps:
   108→      - name: Download all plan statistics
   109→        uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
   110→        continue-on-error: true
   111→        with:
   112→          pattern: plan-stats-*
   113→          path: plan-results/
   114→          merge-multiple: true
   115→
   116→      - name: Generate Summary
   117→        run: |
   118→          echo "## Validation and Plan Summary" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
   119→          echo "" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
   120→
   121→          if [ "${{ needs.detect-changes.outputs.has_changes }}" == "false" ]; then
   122→            echo "No Terraform changes detected" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
   123→            exit 0
   124→          fi
   125→
   126→          # Build results table from plan stats
   127→          SUCCESS_COUNT=0
   128→          FAILURE_COUNT=0
   129→          TOTAL_ADD=0
   130→          TOTAL_CHANGE=0
   131→          TOTAL_DESTROY=0
   132→
   133→          echo "| Environment | Directory | Status | Add | Change | Destroy |" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
   134→          echo "|-------------|-----------|--------|-----|--------|---------|" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
   135→
   136→          if [ -d "plan-results" ]; then
   137→            for statfile in plan-results/plan_stats_*.json; do
   138→              if [ -f "$statfile" ]; then
   139→                DIRECTORY=$(jq -r '.directory' "$statfile")
   140→                ENVIRONMENT=$(jq -r '.environment' "$statfile")
   141→                ADD=$(jq -r '.add' "$statfile")
   142→                CHANGE=$(jq -r '.change' "$statfile")
   143→                DESTROY=$(jq -r '.destroy' "$statfile")
   144→                STATUS=$(jq -r '.status // "success"' "$statfile")
   145→
   146→                if [ "$STATUS" == "success" ]; then
   147→                  SUCCESS_COUNT=$((SUCCESS_COUNT + 1))
   148→                  TOTAL_ADD=$((TOTAL_ADD + ADD))
   149→                  TOTAL_CHANGE=$((TOTAL_CHANGE + CHANGE))
   150→                  TOTAL_DESTROY=$((TOTAL_DESTROY + DESTROY))
   151→                  echo "| ${ENVIRONMENT} | \`${DIRECTORY}\` | Passed | ${ADD} | ${CHANGE} | ${DESTROY} |" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
   152→                else
   153→                  FAILURE_COUNT=$((FAILURE_COUNT + 1))
   154→                  echo "| ${ENVIRONMENT} | \`${DIRECTORY}\` | Failed | - | - | - |" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
   155→                fi
   156→              fi
   157→            done
   158→
   159→            TOTAL_DIRS=$((SUCCESS_COUNT + FAILURE_COUNT))
   160→            echo "| **TOTALS** | | **${SUCCESS_COUNT}/${TOTAL_DIRS}** | **${TOTAL_ADD}** | **${TOTAL_CHANGE}** | **${TOTAL_DESTROY}** |" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
   161→          fi
   162→
   163→          echo "" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
   164→
   165→          if [ "$FAILURE_COUNT" -gt 0 ]; then
   166→            echo "### Status: Failed" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
   167→            echo "Review error logs in failed jobs above" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
   168→          else
   169→            echo "### Status: Ready to merge" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
   170→            echo "All validations passed. Merge and deploy via 'Validate, Plan and Apply' workflow." >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
   171→          fi
   172→
   173→      - name: Check Overall Status
   174→        if: needs.detect-changes.outputs.has_changes == 'true'
   175→        run: |
   176→          if [ "${{ needs.validate.result }}" == "failure" ] || \
   177→             [ "${{ needs.plan.result }}" == "failure" ]; then
   178→            echo "::error::Validation failed. Please review the errors above."
   179→            exit 1
   180→          fi
   181→

    42→          else

    44→            echo "::error::Allowed branches: main, develop, v* tags"
    45→            exit 1
    46→          fi
    47→
    48→          case "$BRANCH_TYPE" in

    50→              if [[ "$ENV" != "prod" ]]; then
    51→                echo "::error::Version tags (v*) can only validate production"
    52→                echo "::error::Current: $BRANCH -> $ENV"

    54→              fi
    55→              ;;
    56→            main)

    67→              fi
    68→              ;;
    69→          esac

    77→

|\" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY\n          elif [ \"$PROD_STATUS\" == \"success\" ]; then\n            echo \"| prod | :warning: Drift detected | +${{ needs.detect-drift-prod.outputs.add_count }} ~${{ needs.detect-drift-prod.outputs.change_count }} -${{ needs.detect-drift-prod.outputs.destroy_count }} |\" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY\n          elif [ \"$PROD_STATUS\" == \"skipped\" ]; then\n            echo \"| prod | :fast_forward: Skipped | - |\" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY\n          else\n            echo \"| prod | :x: Failed | - |\" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY\n          fi\n\n      - name: Create Issue on Drift\n        if: |\n          needs.detect-drift-dev.outputs.changes_detected == 'true' ||\n          needs.detect-drift-qa.outputs.changes_detected == 'true' ||\n          needs.detect-drift-prod.outputs.changes_detected == 'true'\n        uses: actions/github-script@v7\n        with:\n          script: |\n            const devChanges = '${{ needs.detect-drift-dev.outputs.changes_detected }}' === 'true';\n            const qaChanges = '${{ needs.detect-drift-qa.outputs.changes_detected }}' === 'true';\n            const prodChanges = '${{ needs.detect-drift-prod.outputs.changes_detected }}' === 'true';\n\n            let body = '## Terraform Drift Detected\\n\\n';\n            body += 'The nightly drift detection found configuration drift in the following environments:\\n\\n';\n\n            if (devChanges) {\n              body += `- **dev**: +${{ needs.detect-drift-dev.outputs.add_count }} ~${{ needs.detect-drift-dev.outputs.change_count }} -${{ needs.detect-drift-dev.outputs.destroy_count }}\\n`;\n            }\n            if (qaChanges) {\n              body += `- **qa**: +${{ needs.detect-drift-qa.outputs.add_count }} ~${{ needs.detect-drift-qa.outputs.change_count }} -${{ needs.detect-drift-qa.outputs.destroy_count }}\\n`;\n            }\n            if (prodChanges) {\n              body += `- **prod**: +${{ needs.detect-drift-prod.outputs.add_count }} ~${{ needs.detect-drift-prod.outputs.change_count }} -${{ needs.detect-drift-prod.outputs.destroy_count }}\\n`;\n            }\n\n            body += '\\n### Action Required\\n';\n            body += 'Review the [workflow run](' + context.serverUrl + '/' + context.repo.owner + '/' + context.repo.repo + '/actions/runs/' + context.runId + ') for details.\\n\\n';\n            body += 'Either:\\n';\n            body += '1. Apply Terraform to sync infrastructure with code\\n';\n            body += '2. Update code to match current infrastructure state\\n';\n\n            const today = new Date().toISOString().split('T')[0];\n            const title = `Terraform Drift Detected - ${today}`;\n\n            // Check for existing open drift issue\n            const existingIssues = await github.rest.issues.listForRepo({\n              owner: context.repo.owner,\n              repo: context.repo.repo,\n              state: 'open',\n              labels: 'drift-detection'\n            });\n\n            if (existingIssues.data.length === 0) {\n              await github.rest.issues.create({\n                owner: context.repo.owner,\n                repo: context.repo.repo,\n                title: title,\n                body: body,\n                labels: ['drift-detection', 'terraform']\n              });\n            } else {\n              // Update existing issue\n              await github.rest.issues.createComment({\n                owner: context.repo.owner,\n                repo: context.repo.repo,\n                issue_number: existingIssues.data[0].number,\n                body: body\n              });\n            }\n"
}

     1→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
     2→# CrewAI Platform - Dev Environment
     3→#
     4→# Terraform configuration for CrewAI Enterprise deployment on GKE.
     5→# Composes remote modules from kix-platform-modules plus inline resources.
     6→#
     7→# File Organization:
     8→# - main.tf           : Providers, data sources, locals (this file)
     9→# - service-accounts.tf: GCP service account and IAM bindings
    10→# - kubernetes.tf     : Namespaces, K8s service accounts, quotas, limits
    11→# - secrets.tf        : Secret Manager and K8s secrets/configmaps
    12→# - storage.tf        : GCS buckets and HMAC keys
    13→# - database.tf       : Cloud SQL databases, user, and proxy deployment
    14→# - artifact-registry.tf: Container registry for crew builds
    15→# - variables.tf      : Input variable definitions
    16→# - outputs.tf        : Output value definitions
    17→# - versions.tf       : Provider version constraints
    18→# - backend.tf        : Remote state configuration
    19→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    20→
    21→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    22→# Locals
    23→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    24→# Common values used across multiple resources.
    25→
    26→locals {
    27→  # Standard labels applied to all resources for identification and cost tracking
    28→  labels = {
    29→    app         = "crewai"
    30→    environment = var.environment
    31→    managed-by  = "terraform"
    32→    platform    = "crewai"
    33→  }
    34→
    35→  # Construct SA email statically to avoid for_each unknown value issues.
    36→  # Secret-manager modules use depends_on to ensure the SA exists before
    37→  # IAM bindings are created (static email breaks implicit dependency).
    38→  crewai_sa_email = "crewai-platform@${var.gke_project_id}.iam.gserviceaccount.com"
    39→}
    40→
    41→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    42→# Providers
    43→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    44→
    45→provider "google" {
    46→  project = var.gke_project_id
    47→  region  = var.region
    48→}
    49→
    50→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    51→# Data Sources: GKE Cluster for Kubernetes Provider
    52→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    53→# Explicit GKE authentication for reproducible deployments.
    54→# Avoids reliance on KUBECONFIG environment variable.
    55→
    56→data "google_client_config" "default" {}
    57→
    58→data "google_container_cluster" "gke" {
    59→  project  = var.gke_project_id
    60→  name     = var.gke_cluster_name
    61→  location = var.region
    62→}
    63→
    64→provider "kubernetes" {
    65→  host                   = "https://${data.google_container_cluster.gke.endpoint}"
    66→  token                  = data.google_client_config.default.access_token
    67→  cluster_ca_certificate = base64decode(data.google_container_cluster.gke.master_auth[0].cluster_ca_certificate)
    68→}
    69→

     1→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
     2→# Service Accounts and IAM Bindings
     3→#
     4→# GCP service account for CrewAI platform workloads with Workload Identity.
     5→# Includes all IAM bindings for Cloud SQL, GCS, and Artifact Registry access.
     6→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
     7→
     8→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
     9→# GCP Service Account
    10→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    11→# Created inline (not via module) to avoid circular dependencies with HMAC keys
    12→# and secrets that reference the service account email.
    13→
    14→resource "google_service_account" "crewai_platform" {
    15→  project      = var.gke_project_id
    16→  account_id   = "crewai-platform"
    17→  display_name = "CrewAI Platform"
    18→}
    19→
    20→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    21→# IAM: Cloud SQL Access
    22→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    23→# Allows the service account to connect to Cloud SQL via the Cloud SQL Proxy.
    24→
    25→resource "google_project_iam_member" "cloudsql_client" {
    26→  project = var.platform_data_project
    27→  role    = "roles/cloudsql.client"
    28→  member  = "serviceAccount:${google_service_account.crewai_platform.email}"
    29→}
    30→
    31→resource "google_project_iam_member" "cloudsql_instance_user" {
    32→  project = var.platform_data_project
    33→  role    = "roles/cloudsql.instanceUser"
    34→  member  = "serviceAccount:${google_service_account.crewai_platform.email}"
    35→}
    36→
    37→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    38→# IAM: GCS Bucket Access
    39→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    40→# Data bucket: full object admin for reading and writing application data.
    41→# Logs bucket: object creator only for write-only audit logging.
    42→
    43→resource "google_storage_bucket_iam_member" "data_bucket" {
    44→  bucket = module.gcs_data.bucket_name
    45→  role   = "roles/storage.objectAdmin"
    46→  member = "serviceAccount:${google_service_account.crewai_platform.email}"
    47→}
    48→
    49→resource "google_storage_bucket_iam_member" "logs_bucket" {
    50→  bucket = module.gcs_logs.bucket_name
    51→  role   = "roles/storage.objectCreator"
    52→  member = "serviceAccount:${google_service_account.crewai_platform.email}"
    53→}
    54→
    55→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    56→# IAM: Shared Artifact Registry Access
    57→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    58→# Allows the service account to pull container images from the shared
    59→# Artifact Registry repository (crewai-images in kd-ix-eur-shr-artifacts).
    60→# These are the mirrored CrewAI platform images synced from images.crewai.com.
    61→
    62→resource "google_artifact_registry_repository_iam_member" "shared_ar_reader" {
    63→  project    = var.shared_artifacts_project
    64→  location   = var.region
    65→  repository = var.shared_ar_repository
    66→  role       = "roles/artifactregistry.reader"
    67→  member     = "serviceAccount:${google_service_account.crewai_platform.email}"
    68→}
    69→
    70→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    71→# IAM: Secret Manager Access (for External Secrets Operator)
    72→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    73→# Allows the service account to access secrets in Secret Manager.
    74→# Required for ESO to pull secrets and create Kubernetes secrets.
    75→
    76→resource "google_project_iam_member" "secret_accessor" {
    77→  project = var.security_project_id
    78→  role    = "roles/secretmanager.secretAccessor"
    79→  member  = "serviceAccount:${google_service_account.crewai_platform.email}"
    80→}
    81→
    82→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    83→# IAM: Workload Identity Binding
    84→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    85→# Allows the Kubernetes service account to impersonate the GCP service account.
    86→# This enables pods to authenticate to GCP services without service account keys.
    87→
    88→resource "google_service_account_iam_member" "workload_identity" {
    89→  service_account_id = google_service_account.crewai_platform.name
    90→  role               = "roles/iam.workloadIdentityUser"
    91→  member             = "serviceAccount:${var.gke_project_id}.svc.id.goog[crewai/crewai-sa]"
    92→}
    93→
    94→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    95→# IAM: GitHub Actions Impersonation
    96→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    97→# Allows GitHub Actions to impersonate this service account for CI/CD.
    98→# The GitHub service account is created separately in the platform infrastructure.
    99→
   100→resource "google_service_account_iam_member" "github_impersonation" {
   101→  service_account_id = google_service_account.crewai_platform.name
   102→  role               = "roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator"
   103→  member             = "serviceAccount:github-crewai-${var.environment}@${var.gke_project_id}.iam.gserviceaccount.com"
   104→}
   105→

     1→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
     2→# Secrets Management
     3→#
     4→# GCP Secret Manager secrets consumed by External Secrets Operator (ESO).
     5→# ESO syncs secrets from GCP SM to K8s via ExternalSecret + ClusterSecretStore.
     6→# ClusterSecretStore (gcp-secret-manager) is platform-managed - not in this code.
     7→# Uses the single-secret-per-call pattern for the secret-manager module.
     8→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
     9→
    10→# NOTE: Database uses IAM authentication via Cloud SQL Proxy - no password needed
    11→
    12→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    13→# Secret Manager: Rails Secrets
    14→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    15→# SECRET_KEY_BASE for Rails session encryption and signed cookies.
    16→# Replicates Helm chart behavior: 64-character alphanumeric string.
    17→# Terraform state preserves the value across applies (equivalent to Helm's
    18→# existing secret lookup pattern).
    19→#
    20→# ENCRYPTION_KEY for ActiveRecord encryption (hex format, 64 chars = 32 bytes).
    21→#
    22→# Active Record Encryption keys (64 chars each, matching Helm chart):
    23→# - ACTIVE_RECORD_ENCRYPTION_PRIMARY_KEY
    24→# - ACTIVE_RECORD_ENCRYPTION_DETERMINISTIC_KEY
    25→# - ACTIVE_RECORD_ENCRYPTION_KEY_DERIVATION_SALT
    26→
    27→resource "random_password" "rails_secret_key_base" {
    28→  length  = 64
    29→  special = false
    30→}
    31→
    32→resource "random_password" "active_record_encryption_primary_key" {
    33→  length  = 64
    34→  special = false
    35→}
    36→
    37→resource "random_password" "active_record_encryption_deterministic_key" {
    38→  length  = 64
    39→  special = false
    40→}
    41→
    42→resource "random_password" "active_record_encryption_key_derivation_salt" {
    43→  length  = 64
    44→  special = false
    45→}
    46→
    47→resource "random_id" "encryption_key" {
    48→  byte_length = 32
    49→}
    50→
    51→module "secret_rails_secrets" {
    52→  source = "github.com/konecta-ix-platform/kix-platform-modules//terraform/gcp/secret-manager?ref=main"
    53→
    54→  project_id  = var.security_project_id
    55→  environment = var.environment
    56→  secret_id   = "crewai-rails-secrets-${var.environment}"
    57→  secret_data = jsonencode({
    58→    secret_key_base                              = random_password.rails_secret_key_base.result
    59→    encryption_key                               = random_id.encryption_key.hex
    60→    active_record_encryption_primary_key         = random_password.active_record_encryption_primary_key.result
    61→    active_record_encryption_deterministic_key   = random_password.active_record_encryption_deterministic_key.result
    62→    active_record_encryption_key_derivation_salt = random_password.active_record_encryption_key_derivation_salt.result
    63→  })
    64→
    65→  accessor_service_accounts = [local.crewai_sa_email]
    66→  additional_labels         = local.labels
    67→
    68→  depends_on = [google_service_account.crewai_platform]
    69→}
    70→
    71→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    72→# Secret Manager: GCS Credentials (HMAC Keys)
    73→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    74→# HMAC keys for S3-compatible GCS access (used by Rails ActiveStorage).
    75→
    76→module "secret_gcs_credentials" {
    77→  source = "github.com/konecta-ix-platform/kix-platform-modules//terraform/gcp/secret-manager?ref=main"
    78→
    79→  project_id  = var.security_project_id
    80→  environment = var.environment
    81→  secret_id   = "crewai-gcs-credentials-${var.environment}"
    82→  secret_data = jsonencode({
    83→    access_key_id     = google_storage_hmac_key.crewai.access_id
    84→    secret_access_key = google_storage_hmac_key.crewai.secret
    85→  })
    86→
    87→  accessor_service_accounts = [local.crewai_sa_email]
    88→  additional_labels         = local.labels
    89→
    90→  depends_on = [google_service_account.crewai_platform]
    91→}
    92→
    93→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    94→# Secret Manager: WorkOS OAuth Credentials
    95→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    96→# WorkOS authentication credentials for SSO integration.
    97→# Note: These are development/staging credentials.
    98→
    99→module "secret_workos_credentials" {
   100→  source = "github.com/konecta-ix-platform/kix-platform-modules//terraform/gcp/secret-manager?ref=main"
   101→
   102→  project_id  = var.security_project_id
   103→  environment = var.environment
   104→  secret_id   = "crewai-workos-credentials-${var.environment}"
   105→  secret_data = jsonencode({
   106→    client_id       = var.oauth_client_id
   107→    api_key         = var.oauth_api_key
   108→    cookie_password = var.oauth_cookie_password
   109→    authkit_domain  = var.oauth_domain
   110→  })
   111→
   112→  accessor_service_accounts = [local.crewai_sa_email]
   113→  additional_labels         = local.labels
   114→
   115→  depends_on = [google_service_account.crewai_platform]
   116→}
   117→
   118→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   119→# Secret Manager: GitHub App Credentials
   120→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   121→# GitHub App credentials for repository integration.
   122→# Note: These are development credentials for the crewai-git-dev GitHub App.
   123→
   124→module "secret_github_credentials" {
   125→  source = "github.com/konecta-ix-platform/kix-platform-modules//terraform/gcp/secret-manager?ref=main"
   126→
   127→  project_id  = var.security_project_id
   128→  environment = var.environment
   129→  secret_id   = "crewai-github-credentials-${var.environment}"
   130→  secret_data = jsonencode({
   131→    client_secret   = var.github_client_secret
   132→    app_private_key = var.github_app_private_key
   133→  })
   134→
   135→  accessor_service_accounts = [local.crewai_sa_email]
   136→  additional_labels         = local.labels
   137→
   138→  depends_on = [google_service_account.crewai_platform]
   139→}
   140→
   141→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   142→# Secret Manager: Replicated SDK Credentials
   143→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   144→# Replicated SDK auth token for license validation and update checks.
   145→
   146→module "secret_replicated_credentials" {
   147→  source = "github.com/konecta-ix-platform/kix-platform-modules//terraform/gcp/secret-manager?ref=main"
   148→
   149→  project_id  = var.security_project_id
   150→  environment = var.environment
   151→  secret_id   = "crewai-replicated-credentials-${var.environment}"
   152→  secret_data = jsonencode({
   153→    auth_token = var.replicated_auth_token
   154→  })
   155→
   156→  accessor_service_accounts = [local.crewai_sa_email]
   157→  additional_labels         = local.labels
   158→
   159→  depends_on = [google_service_account.crewai_platform]
   160→}
   161→
   162→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   163→# ExternalSecret: CrewAI Application Credentials
   164→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   165→# Uses ClusterSecretStore (platform-managed) to sync secrets from GCP SM.
   166→# ESO creates the K8s secret automatically - no direct secret creation needed.
   167→# The ClusterSecretStore 'gcp-secret-manager' is managed at platform level.
   168→#
   169→# Requires: External Secrets Operator CRD (external-secrets.io/v1beta1)
   170→# If ESO is not yet installed, set var.eso_installed = false to skip this
   171→# resource during initial cluster bootstrap, then re-apply after ESO is deployed.
   172→
   173→resource "kubernetes_manifest" "external_secret_crewai_credentials" {
   174→  count = var.eso_installed ? 1 : 0
   175→
   176→  manifest = {
   177→    apiVersion = "external-secrets.io/v1beta1"
   178→    kind       = "ExternalSecret"
   179→    metadata = {
   180→      name      = "crewai-credentials"
   181→      namespace = local.platform_namespace
   182→      labels = {
   183→        app         = "crewai"
   184→        environment = var.environment
   185→        managed-by  = "terraform"
   186→      }
   187→    }
   188→    spec = {
   189→      refreshInterval = "1h"
   190→      secretStoreRef = {
   191→        kind = "ClusterSecretStore"
   192→        name = "gcp-secret-manager"
   193→      }
   194→      target = {
   195→        name           = "crewai-secrets"
   196→        creationPolicy = "Owner"
   197→      }
   198→      data = [
   199→        {
   200→          secretKey = "SECRET_KEY_BASE"
   201→          remoteRef = {
   202→            key      = "crewai-rails-secrets-${var.environment}"
   203→            property = "secret_key_base"
   204→          }
   205→        },
   206→        {
   207→          secretKey = "ENCRYPTION_KEY"
   208→          remoteRef = {
   209→            key      = "crewai-rails-secrets-${var.environment}"
   210→            property = "encryption_key"
   211→          }
   212→        },
   213→        {
   214→          secretKey = "ACTIVE_RECORD_ENCRYPTION_PRIMARY_KEY"
   215→          remoteRef = {
   216→            key      = "crewai-rails-secrets-${var.environment}"
   217→            property = "active_record_encryption_primary_key"
   218→          }
   219→        },
   220→        {
   221→          secretKey = "ACTIVE_RECORD_ENCRYPTION_DETERMINISTIC_KEY"
   222→          remoteRef = {
   223→            key      = "crewai-rails-secrets-${var.environment}"
   224→            property = "active_record_encryption_deterministic_key"
   225→          }
   226→        },
   227→        {
   228→          secretKey = "ACTIVE_RECORD_ENCRYPTION_KEY_DERIVATION_SALT"
   229→          remoteRef = {
   230→            key      = "crewai-rails-secrets-${var.environment}"
   231→            property = "active_record_encryption_key_derivation_salt"
   232→          }
   233→        },
   234→        {
   235→          secretKey = "AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID"
   236→          remoteRef = {
   237→            key      = "crewai-gcs-credentials-${var.environment}"
   238→            property = "access_key_id"
   239→          }
   240→        },
   241→        {
   242→          secretKey = "AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY"
   243→          remoteRef = {
   244→            key      = "crewai-gcs-credentials-${var.environment}"
   245→            property = "secret_access_key"
   246→          }
   247→        },
   248→        {
   249→          secretKey = "WORKOS_CLIENT_ID"
   250→          remoteRef = {
   251→            key      = "crewai-workos-credentials-${var.environment}"
   252→            property = "client_id"
   253→          }
   254→        },
   255→        {
   256→          secretKey = "WORKOS_API_KEY"
   257→          remoteRef = {
   258→            key      = "crewai-workos-credentials-${var.environment}"
   259→            property = "api_key"
   260→          }
   261→        },
   262→        {
   263→          secretKey = "WORKOS_COOKIE_PASSWORD"
   264→          remoteRef = {
   265→            key      = "crewai-workos-credentials-${var.environment}"
   266→            property = "cookie_password"
   267→          }
   268→        },
   269→        {
   270→          secretKey = "WORKOS_AUTHKIT_DOMAIN"
   271→          remoteRef = {
   272→            key      = "crewai-workos-credentials-${var.environment}"
   273→            property = "authkit_domain"
   274→          }
   275→        },
   276→        {
   277→          secretKey = "GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET"
   278→          remoteRef = {
   279→            key      = "crewai-github-credentials-${var.environment}"
   280→            property = "client_secret"
   281→          }

   283→        {
   284→          secretKey = "GITHUB_APP_PRIVATE_KEY"

Here's what's happening:

**The error:** BuildKit is trying to pull base image `crewai-enterprise-preinstalled-v2` from the shared AR (`kd-ix-eur-shr-artifacts/crewai-images`) during a crew build. The key phrase is **"fetch anonymous token"** — BuildKit is sending no credentials at all.

**Why:** There are two distinct image-pull mechanisms:

| Context | Who pulls | Auth source |
|---------|-----------|-------------|
| Pod startup (kubelet) | GKE node pool SA | Node pool config — works |
| Crew build (BuildKit daemon) | BuildKit process inside pod | BuildKit's own registry auth — **missing** |

The IAM is fine — `crewai-platform` SA has `artifactregistry.reader` on the shared AR. The problem is that BuildKit doesn't automatically use Workload Identity to authenticate when pulling base images during builds. Even with `automountServiceAccountToken: true`, BuildKit's OCI worker doesn't leverage the GKE metadata server for Docker registry auth.

On Autopilot with rootless mode this likely worked because the Autopilot node SA had broader AR access that applied at the node level, or rootless BuildKit used the kubelet credential chain differently.

Let me check if the upstream chart exposes a BuildKit registry auth config.

Now I have comprehensive research. Let me compile the final report.

---

## Research Summary

This research investigates how BuildKit authenticates to Google Artifact Registry (GAR) when running as a long-lived daemon pod on GKE with Workload Identity. The core finding is that **BuildKit does NOT automatically use GKE Workload Identity / metadata server credentials for registry authentication**. BuildKit's architecture relies on either client-side session-based credential forwarding or daemon-side Docker config.json -- neither of which natively integrates with GCP's metadata server for registry token acquisition. The 403 "failed to fetch anonymous token" error confirms that BuildKit is making unauthenticated requests to the GAR token endpoint.

---

## Implementation Solutions

### Recommended Approach: `buildkit.dockerConfigSecret` with Init Container Token Injection

```yaml
# CrewAI Helm values pattern using the chart's native dockerConfigSecret support
# SOURCE: https://enterprise-docs.crewai.com/reference/chart-values/buildkit.md

# PATTERN: Init container generates short-lived OAuth2 token from GKE metadata server,
# writes it as Docker config.json, stores in a shared volume that BuildKit reads.
# WHY: BuildKit daemon cannot natively use GKE Workload Identity for registry auth.

# Step 1: Generate config.json with OAuth2 token from metadata server
# This would run in an init container or CronJob:
#   ACCESS_TOKEN=$(curl -s -H "Metadata-Flavor: Google" \
#     "http://metadata.google.internal/computeMetadata/v1/instance/service-accounts/default/token" \
#     | jq -r '.access_token')
#
#   cat > /docker-config/.dockerconfigjson <<EOF
#   {
#     "auths": {
#       "europe-west1-docker.pkg.dev": {
#         "username": "oauth2accesstoken",
#         "password": "$ACCESS_TOKEN"
#       }
#     }
#   }
#   EOF

# Step 2: Create K8s secret from the generated config
#   kubectl create secret docker-registry buildkit-ar-creds \
#     --docker-server=europe-west1-docker.pkg.dev \
#     --docker-username=oauth2accesstoken \
#     --docker-password="$ACCESS_TOKEN" \
#     --namespace=crewai-crews-dev

# Step 3: Reference in CrewAI Helm values
# buildkit:
#   dockerConfigSecret=[REDACTED]"
```

### Alternative Approaches

```yaml
# ALTERNATIVE 1: Custom BuildKit Image with docker-credential-gcr
# SOURCE: https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/docker-credential-gcr
# WHEN TO USE: When you want fully automatic, zero-maintenance credential refresh
# PROS: Automatic token refresh via metadata server, no token expiry issues
# CONS: Requires building/maintaining a custom BuildKit image with credential helper binary
#
# Dockerfile for custom BuildKit image:
#   FROM moby/buildkit:latest
#   COPY --from=gcr.io/cloud-builders/docker-credential-gcr /usr/bin/docker-credential-gcr /usr/bin/
#   RUN mkdir -p /root/.docker && \
#       docker-credential-gcr configure-docker --registries=europe-west1-docker.pkg.dev
#
# config.json result:
#   {
#     "credHelpers": {
#       "europe-west1-docker.pkg.dev": "gcr"
#     }
#   }
#
# CRITICAL: docker-credential-gcr v2.1.0+ required for Workload Identity support
# The credential helper fetches tokens from the GKE metadata server automatically

# ALTERNATIVE 2: CronJob-based Token Rotation
# SOURCE: https://docs.cloud.google.com/artifact-registry/docs/docker/authentication
# WHEN TO USE: Simplest approach; acceptable if builds are not continuous 24/7
# PROS: No custom images needed, uses standard K8s primitives
# CONS: Token expires after 60 minutes; requires CronJob to refresh every ~45 minutes
#       If CronJob fails, builds will fail until next successful rotation
#
# CronJob runs every 45 minutes:
#   1. Curls metadata server for access token
#   2. Deletes and recreates docker-registry secret
#   3. BuildKit picks up new creds on next build

# ALTERNATIVE 3: Sidecar Container Token Refresher
# WHEN TO USE: Continuous build environments where token must never expire
# PROS: Always-fresh credentials, no downtime window
# CONS: Additional complexity, extra container running alongside buildkitd
#
# Sidecar pattern:
#   1. Sidecar container with gcloud SDK or curl + jq
#   2. Runs in a loop: fetch token, write config.json to shared emptyDir volume
#   3. BuildKit reads config.json from the shared volume
#   4. Sleep interval: 50 minutes (token valid for 60 min)
```

## Documentation Research

### Critical Documentation Links

- **Primary Docs**: [Google Artifact Registry Docker Authentication](https://docs.cloud.google.com/artifact-registry/docs/docker/authentication) -- covers oauth2accesstoken approach, credential helpers, and access token authentication
- **Credential Helper**: [docker-credential-gcr README](https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/docker-credential-gcr/blob/master/README.md) -- standalone credential helper that auto-discovers credentials from GKE metadata server
- **CrewAI BuildKit Config**: [CrewAI Enterprise BuildKit Chart Values](https://enterprise-docs.crewai.com/reference/chart-values/buildkit.md) -- `dockerConfigSecret` and `registries` configuration
- **CrewAI Private Registry**: [CrewAI Private Registry Setup](https://enterprise-docs.crewai.com/configuration/private-registry.md) -- air-gapped/private registry mirroring guide
- **BuildKit Auth Architecture**: [BuildKit PR #1660 - Client-side token fetching](https://github.com/moby/buildkit/pull/1660) -- explains session-based auth model
- **BuildKit K8s Examples**: [BuildKit Kubernetes Examples](https://github.com/moby/buildkit/tree/master/examples/kubernetes) -- official Kubernetes deployment patterns
- **GKE Workload Identity**: [GKE Workload Identity Setup](https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/workload-identity) -- binding K8s SA to GCP SA
- **BuildKit Token Expiry Bug**: [moby/buildkit#5712](https://github.com/moby/buildkit/issues/5712) -- tokens not refreshed during long builds

### Library Integration Patterns

```bash
# docker-credential-gcr installation (for custom BuildKit image approach)
# Download from: https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/docker-credential-gcr/releases
# CRITICAL: Must be v2.1.0+ for Workload Identity Federation support

# Configure for Artifact Registry (pkg.dev domains):
docker-credential-gcr configure-docker --registries=europe-west1-docker.pkg.dev

# Verify credential helper works from within the container:
echo "https://europe-west1-docker.pkg.dev" | docker-credential-gcr get
# Should return JSON with "Secret" field containing an access token

# Credential search order:
# 1. Private credential store (gcr-login)
# 2. GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS env var
# 3. Default ADC locations (~/.config/gcloud/application_default_credentials.json)
# 4. GCE/GKE metadata server (Workload Identity token)
```

## Business Logic Research

### Industry Standards

- **Common Pattern**: OAuth2 access token injection via init container or sidecar -- used by Jenkins X, GitLab CI/CD runners on GKE, Concourse CI, Argo CD
- **User Expectations**: Container builds should authenticate transparently using pod-level Workload Identity without manual secret management
- **Business Rules**: Access tokens expire after 60 minutes; any solution must handle token rotation for builds that may queue or run longer than 1 hour
- **Kubernetes v1.33 Direction**: Native workload-identity-based image pulls are in alpha ([KEP](https://kubernetes.io/blog/2025/05/07/kubernetes-v1-33-wi-for-image-pulls/)), but this only covers kubelet image pulls, not BuildKit internal image pulls

### Integration Requirements

- **Data Flow**: GKE metadata server -> OAuth2 access token -> Docker config.json -> BuildKit daemon -> GAR v2/token endpoint -> registry pull
- **State Management**: Access tokens are ephemeral (60-minute TTL); the Docker config.json secret or volume must be refreshed before expiry
- **Error Scenarios**:
  - Token expired mid-build: BuildKit does not refresh tokens during a build ([moby/buildkit#5712](https://github.com/moby/buildkit/issues/5712))
  - Metadata server unreachable: GKE metadata server requires `iam.gke.io/gke-metadata-server-enabled: "true"` on the node pool
  - IAM binding missing: 403 at v2/token endpoint when GCP SA lacks `artifactregistry.repositories.downloadArtifacts`
  - Node access scopes insufficient: Cluster must have `cloud-platform` or `storage-ro` scope

## Implementation Examples from Research

### Production Examples

```bash
# EXAMPLE 1: Metadata server token fetch (from within a GKE pod with Workload Identity)
# SOURCE: https://docs.cloud.google.com/artifact-registry/docs/docker/authentication

ACCESS_TOKEN=$(curl -s \
  -H "Metadata-Flavor: Google" \
  "http://metadata.google.internal/computeMetadata/v1/instance/service-accounts/default/token" \
  | jq -r '.access_token')

# Create Docker config.json for BuildKit
cat > /root/.docker/config.json <<EOF
{
  "auths": {
    "europe-west1-docker.pkg.dev": {
      "auth": "$(echo -n "oauth2accesstoken:${ACCESS_TOKEN}" | base64)"
    }
  }
}
EOF
```

```bash
# EXAMPLE 2: Kubernetes secret creation for BuildKit dockerConfigSecret
# SOURCE: https://enterprise-docs.crewai.com/reference/chart-values/buildkit.md

# Fetch token from metadata server
ACCESS_TOKEN=$(curl -s -H "Metadata-Flavor: Google" \
  "http://metadata.google.internal/computeMetadata/v1/instance/service-accounts/default/token" \
  | jq -r '.access_token')

# Create docker-registry secret
kubectl create secret docker-registry buildkit-ar-creds \
  --docker-server=europe-west1-docker.pkg.dev \
  --docker-username=oauth2accesstoken \
  --docker-password="${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  --namespace=crewai-crews-dev \
  --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
```

```yaml
# EXAMPLE 3: CrewAI Helm values with dockerConfigSecret
# SOURCE: https://enterprise-docs.crewai.com/reference/chart-values/buildkit.md

buildkit:
  dockerConfigSecret=[REDACTED]"
  registries:
    - hostname: "europe-west1-docker.pkg.dev"
      http: false
      insecure: false
```

### Testing Patterns

```bash
# TEST APPROACH: Verify BuildKit can authenticate to Artifact Registry
# SOURCE: https://docs.cloud.google.com/artifact-registry/docs/docker/authentication

# 1. Verify Workload Identity binding
kubectl exec -it <buildkit-pod> -n crewai-crews-dev -- \
  curl -s -H "Metadata-Flavor: Google" \
  "http://metadata.google.internal/computeMetadata/v1/instance/service-accounts/default/email"
# Expected: <gcp-sa>@<project>.iam.gserviceaccount.com

# 2. Verify token can be fetched
kubectl exec -it <buildkit-pod> -n crewai-crews-dev -- \
  curl -s -H "Metadata-Flavor: Google" \
  "http://metadata.google.internal/computeMetadata/v1/instance/service-accounts/default/token" \
  | jq '.access_token | length'
# Expected: non-zero number

# 3. Verify GAR token endpoint accepts the access token
ACCESS_TOKEN=$(kubectl exec -it <buildkit-pod> -n crewai-crews-dev -- \
  curl -s -H "Metadata-Flavor: Google" \
  "http://metadata.google.internal/computeMetadata/v1/instance/service-accounts/default/token" \
  | jq -r '.access_token')

curl -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  "https://europe-west1-docker.pkg.dev/v2/token?scope=repository:kd-ix-eur-shr-artifacts/crewai-images/crewai-enterprise-preinstalled-v2:pull&service=europe-west1-docker.pkg.dev"
# Expected: JSON with access_token, NOT 403

# 4. Verify IAM permissions
gcloud artifacts repositories get-iam-policy crewai-images \
  --project=kd-ix-eur-shr-artifacts \
  --location=europe-west1
# Expected: GCP SA has roles/artifactregistry.reader
```

## Best Practices and Pitfalls

### Critical Gotchas

- **AVOID**: Assuming BuildKit auto-discovers GKE Workload Identity credentials. BuildKit's `buildkitd` daemon does NOT query the GKE metadata server for registry authentication. It only reads Docker config.json or receives credentials from a buildctl client session. (Source: [moby/buildkit#2136](https://github.com/moby/buildkit/issues/2136), [moby/buildkit#5762](https://github.com/moby/buildkit/issues/5762))

- **AVOID**: Using the `auth` field in config.json with older BuildKit versions. BuildKit historically ignored the base64-encoded `auth` field and only recognized explicit `username` and `password` fields. (Source: [moby/buildkit#2136](https://github.com/moby/buildkit/issues/2136))

- **SECURITY**: OAuth2 access tokens expire after 60 minutes. If using static token injection, builds queued for longer than 60 minutes will fail with 401/403 errors. BuildKit does NOT refresh tokens mid-build. (Source: [moby/buildkit#5712](https://github.com/moby/buildkit/issues/5712))

- **PERFORMANCE**: The `docker-credential-gcr` standalone helper is significantly faster than the `gcloud` CLI credential helper for automated environments. (Source: [Google Artifact Registry docs](https://docs.cloud.google.com/artifact-registry/docs/docker/authentication))

- **VERSION**: `docker-credential-gcr` must be v2.1.0+ to support Workload Identity Federation (`external_account` credential type). Older versions fail with "unknown credential type: external_account". (Source: [GoogleCloudPlatform/docker-credential-gcr#119](https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/docker-credential-gcr/issues/119))

- **AVOID**: Mounting credentials only as imagePullSecrets on the K8s service account. This only authenticates kubelet for pulling the BuildKit pod image itself -- it does NOT propagate into the builds running within the BuildKit container. (Source: [moby/buildkit#5762](https://github.com/moby/buildkit/issues/5762))

- **NODE CONFIG**: GKE node pools must have the metadata server enabled (`iam.gke.io/gke-metadata-server-enabled: "true"`) and sufficient OAuth scopes (`cloud-platform` or `storage-ro`) for Workload Identity to function. (Source: [GKE Workload Identity docs](https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/workload-identity))

### Best Practices

- **PATTERN**: Use the `credHelpers` approach with `docker-credential-gcr` baked into a custom BuildKit image. This provides automatic, on-demand token refresh from the metadata server without any external token rotation mechanism. (Source: [docker-credential-gcr README](https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/docker-credential-gcr/blob/master/README.md))

- **VALIDATION**: Before deploying, exec into the BuildKit pod and verify metadata server connectivity and token acquisition using `curl -H "Metadata-Flavor: Google" http://metadata.google.internal/computeMetadata/v1/instance/service-accounts/default/token`. (Source: [GKE Workload Identity docs](https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/workload-identity))

- **OPTIMIZATION**: For the `dockerConfigSecret` approach, the CrewAI chart mounts the secret at the daemon level, which is the correct placement since BuildKit's daemon does the actual registry I/O. Client-side session auth is not applicable when CrewAI's internal components trigger builds via the BuildKit API. (Source: [enterprise-docs.crewai.com](https://enterprise-docs.crewai.com/reference/chart-values/buildkit.md))

- **PATTERN**: Use `docker-registry` type K8s secrets (not `Opaque`) for `dockerConfigSecret`, as they automatically produce the `.dockerconfigjson` key that BuildKit expects. (Source: [enterprise-docs.crewai.com](https://enterprise-docs.crewai.com/reference/chart-values/buildkit.md))

### Key External Context Summary

- **Primary Solution**: Inject a Docker config.json into BuildKit via the `buildkit.dockerConfigSecret` Helm value, populated with an OAuth2 access token fetched from the GKE metadata server using `oauth2accesstoken` as the username
- **Critical Setup**: BuildKit does NOT auto-discover Workload Identity credentials -- explicit credential injection is mandatory
- **Main Gotcha**: OAuth2 access tokens expire after 60 minutes AND BuildKit does not refresh tokens mid-build, requiring external rotation and builds that complete within the token window
- **Validation**: Exec into BuildKit pod, curl metadata server for token, then test the GAR v2/token endpoint directly with Bearer auth header

## Integration Instructions

### Key Research Findings Summary
- **Primary Solution**: Use `buildkit.dockerConfigSecret` CrewAI Helm value pointing to a `docker-registry` K8s secret containing an OAuth2 access token from the GKE metadata server
- **Critical Dependencies**: `docker-credential-gcr` v2.1.0+ (if using credential helper approach), `curl` + `jq` (if using token injection approach)
- **Main Configuration**: `buildkit.dockerConfigSecret=[REDACTED]"` in Helm values.yaml
- **Breaking Changes**: BuildKit token expiry bug (moby/buildkit#5712) means tokens are never refreshed mid-build

### Critical Findings for PRP Integration

1. **Root Cause of the 403**: BuildKit's `buildkitd` daemon makes an anonymous GET request to `https://europe-west1-docker.pkg.dev/v2/token?scope=...` because it has no registry credentials configured. Despite running on GKE with Workload Identity, BuildKit does not query the metadata server for registry authentication. The "failed to fetch anonymous token: 403 Forbidden" message literally means "attempted anonymous auth, was denied."

2. **Why Workload Identity Alone Is Insufficient**: BuildKit's auth architecture is designed around Docker's config.json credential model (either `auths` with static credentials or `credHelpers` with credential helper binaries). It does not implement GCP-specific credential discovery. Workload Identity provides credentials to the pod via the metadata server, but the pod's application must actively request them -- BuildKit does not.

3. **CrewAI's Built-in Mechanism**: The CrewAI Enterprise Helm chart exposes `buildkit.dockerConfigSecret` which mounts a K8s secret as Docker config.json inside the BuildKit daemon container. This is the correct integration point.

4. **Token Lifecycle Concern**: GCP OAuth2 access tokens expire after 60 minutes. BuildKit does not refresh tokens during a build. Any solution must either: (a) use a credential helper that fetches fresh tokens on each registry request, or (b) rotate the secret externally before expiry.

5. **Two Viable Approaches**:
   - **Quick fix**: CronJob-based token rotation into a `docker-registry` K8s secret, referenced by `buildkit.dockerConfigSecret`
   - **Robust fix**: Custom BuildKit image with `docker-credential-gcr` installed and configured for `europe-west1-docker.pkg.dev`, which transparently fetches tokens from the metadata server on each registry interaction

# BuildKit Helm Chart Registry Authentication Configuration

## Key Registry Authentication Parameters

**Image Pull Secret:**
```yaml
buildkit:
  image:
    pullSecret: ""  # Defaults to global image.pullSecret if empty
```

**Docker Registry Secret:**
```yaml
buildkit:
  dockerConfigSecret: "docker-registry"
```

This parameter specifies the Kubernetes secret containing Docker credentials. The secret requires a `.dockerconfigjson` key with base64-encoded Docker configuration.

**Creation Example:**
```bash
kubectl create secret docker-registry buildkit-registry-creds \
  --docker-server=registry.company.com \
  --docker-username=user \
  --docker-password=pass
```

## Registry Configuration

**Mirror and Insecure Registry Setup:**
```yaml
buildkit:
  registries:
    - hostname: "registry.company.com"
      http: false
      insecure: false
      mirrors:
        - "mirror1.company.com"
        - "mirror2.company.com"
    - hostname: "localhost:30000"
      http: true
      insecure: true
```

**Configuration Fields:**
- `hostname`: Registry address
- `http`: HTTP protocol instead of HTTPS
- `insecure`: Skip TLS verification
- `mirrors`: Pull-through cache registries

**Use Cases:**
Internal registries, registry mirrors for acceleration, and air-gapped environments.

## Image Registry Fallback

When `buildkit.image.host` is unset, the chart automatically uses `global.imageRegistry` as the default container registry source.
